chunks: And Ḥafṣ ibn al-Bakhtarī narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

It is appropriate for the Imam to sit until those behind him complete their salat (prayer). It is also appropriate for the Imam to make the tashahhud audible to those behind him, while they do not make anything audible to him, meaning the two testimonies. And he should also make audible to them: 'Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah.'

key_terms.التَّشَهُّدَ: the testimony recited in the sitting of prayer
key_terms.السَّلَامُ عَلَيْنَا وَ عَلَى عِبَادِ ال: the salutation recited in prayer: peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah
key_terms.الشَّهَادَتَيْنِ: the two testimonies of faith within the tashahhud
key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the prayer leader in congregational salat (prayer)
key_terms.يَجْلِسَ: to remain seated after completing the prayer

ai.seo_question: What should the Imam recite aloud in congregational prayer, and should he wait for the followers to finish?
ai.summary: This hadith gives guidance on etiquette and practice in congregational salat (prayer), especially concerning the Imam’s conduct after completing his own prayer and the audibility of parts of the tashahhud. It indicates that the Imam should remain seated until the followers finish and should recite certain portions audibly for them, while they should not recite back audibly to him.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1190 - Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) who said:

"It is appropriate for the Imam to sit until those behind him complete their prayers. The Imam should also recite the tashahhud (testimony of faith) loud enough for those behind him to hear, but they should not make their recitation audible to him—referring to the two testimonies (Shahadatayn). He should also audibly recite 'Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah (swt).'"
